proposals: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should publish monthly Vahan registrations of goods vehicles by fuel type, with LNG shown as its own category, so the size of India's LNG-truck fleet, put at about 1,309 at end-2025, comes from an official series rather than industry estimates.

PNGRB should publish a quarterly list of LNG retail dispensing stations showing which are operating, which have shut, and their monthly sales, so station closures for lack of truck traffic are documented and corridor-first and station-first rollouts can be compared on utilisation.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish the reasons and review conditions for the state-run refiners' 2026 pause in LNG retail expansion, so it is clear what fleet size or station throughput would justify resuming it.

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should publish type-approval emission results, including nitrogen oxides, for LNG and comparable diesel heavy trucks, so any future decision on transport-sector LNG incentives can weigh the higher NOx the post reports against a total cost of ownership close to diesel's.
